subject: Dedicated capacity saturation: fallback audit and customer summary
messages:
From: Skymart Ops <ops@skymart.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@skymart.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05 08:47:00 +01:00
Subject: Spike at 03:40UTC — sustained errors / degraded throughput

Hi Neha,

We observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses and token latency from our dedicated pool starting ~03:40 UTC this morning. The service degraded for ~28 minutes before traffic normalized. This caused timeouts in our inference pipeline and queue buildup.

Can you share an initial explanation for what happened and whether automatic fallback and canary routing were triggered? We rely on the dedicated pool for low-latency inference and need the incident timeline and any evidence for our security/compliance review.

Thanks,
Sam — Skymart Ops

Attachments: (none)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Skymart Ops <ops@skymart.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Chen <laura@skymart.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05 09:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Spike at 03:40UTC — sustained errors / degraded throughput

Hi Sam / Laura —

Thanks for flagging this. Short summary up front: we saw a rapid concurrency surge against your reserved GPU pool that coincided with an autoscaler slow-path; the autoscaler made a scale decision but the new nodes failed to join quickly due to a transient provisioning race, which produced a 20–30s window where request queuing caused elevated 5xx and token latency. Automatic fallback (regional routing to a cold warm-standby / compatible model) started at 03:48 UTC but was rate-limited by your configured strict routing policy, which limited throughput recovery until we intervened.

What we are sending now: an evidence packet with a compact audit (redwood_fallback_audit_20261105.csv), a timeline PDF (saturation_timeline_20261105.pdf), and a short diff showing the autoscaler state (config-diff-autoscaler.txt). Those files include per-request routing decisions, kernel-level errors from the runtime, and timestamps for node join events.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Temporarily relaxed the strict-routing policy on your tenant to allow faster fallback to the warm standby (03:50 UTC).
- Forced a manual scale-up of the reserved pool and validated node join success (03:55 UTC).
- Throttled background batch jobs to reduce contention while nodes warmed.

Next steps we propose (detailed in the attachments):
1) A postmortem call — propose 2026-11-06 10:00 CET.
2) Small policy change: allow a controlled percentage of overflow to warm-standby during critical saturation windows (we include a suggested policy in the PDF).
3) Follow-up hardening: autoscaler pre-warm tweaks and provisioning race fixes; ETA for a patch in our will be included in the postmortem.

We will also propose a one-time service credit for the minutes of degraded throughput; Ben will follow up on commercial credit.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts your SLAs. We will bring a concise action plan on the call.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_fallback_audit_20261105.csv; saturation_timeline_20261105.pdf; config-diff-autoscaler.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Skymart Ops <ops@skymart.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Chen <laura@skymart.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05 12:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Spike at 03:40UTC — saturation findings and remediation plan

Hi Sam / Laura —

Following Neha's summary, a few additional technical observations from our infra team:

- Root cause: a provisioning race in our cloud orchestrator combined with a rare kubelet timeout. When the autoscaler requested 6 additional nodes, 2 nodes entered a pending provisioning state and their join handshake timed out repeatedly for ~90s. That delay is what caused the queuing and elevated errors.

- Fallback behavior: the warm-standby routing path functioned as designed, but your tenant-level policy prevented more than 15% of overflow to be routed to warm-standby. That value was too restrictive for the observed surge magnitude.

- Evidence notes: the CSV contains each request's routing decision; the PDF contains a compact timeline and the exact stove-pipe where queue depth reached threshold. The config-diff includes the autoscaler state at 03:30 vs 03:50.

Action items we will deliver before the postmortem call:
A. Patch the orchestrator join handshake to reduce retry backoff (hotfix candidate: 2026-11-09).
B. Provide a safe tenant policy change that increases warm-standby overflow to 35% during sustained spikes, with a 5-minute cool-down. We will run this as a canary on a small subset of tenants and share results.
C. Commercial: Ben will propose a credit for the 28-minute impact window; we aim to send a formal credit note by 2026-11-06 EOD.

Proposed postmortem agenda (10/06): 15m incident timeline & customer impact; 20m root cause & mitigations; 15m policy changes & rollout plan; 10m Q&A/next steps.

If that time works, we will send a calendar invite and include the SRE and product owners.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_fallback_audit_20261105.csv; saturation_timeline_20261105.pdf; config-diff-autoscaler.txt
From: Laura Chen <laura@skymart.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Skymart Ops <ops@skymart.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06 14:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Spike at 03:40UTC — saturation findings and remediation plan

Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick analysis and for the attachments; the timeline PDF is especially helpful. The proposed 2026-11-06 10:00 CET postmortem conflicted with a company all-hands, but we can meet at 2026-11-06 16:00 CET instead.

A couple quick asks before the call:
- Please include the exact request IDs for the 5 highest-latency samples.
- Confirm whether the patch will require tenant downtime or any config changes on our side.

We appreciate the proactive credit offer; will wait for Ben's note.

Regards,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Skymart AI
